means: Platform host that embeds its own wasm engine and binds every contract natively, so no JavaScript value crosses a contract call.
Platform realised as a layer over a browser engine; wasm components run there and contracts bind through JavaScript glue at the edge.
The set of wasm features and binding conventions a contract binding may assume of a guest and its engine.
Paper check naming which contract operations carry each field of a real harness record shape, or recording a shape gap.
A field or behaviour of a real record shape no contract operation carries; written as a hypothesis with its cost, not as a new contract.
The option picked provisionally from the project md files with its reason and a flip condition; a hypothesis, not a decision.

name: Q2 working choice: embedder for the data-path contracts
claim: Clock, stream, store, module and identity bind natively in an embedder with zero JavaScript values per call; the surface binding stays open between native and adapter. Refuted if M2.1 shows crossings or M2.2 needs more than four native surface capabilities.

name: Q3 working choice: separate product, seams described only
claim: The platform lives apart from the harness and reads its records over file and git protocols; harness seams are written as contract records without binding. Refuted if the ledger app needs a harness code change or seam coverage is under ten of thirteen.

name: Q9 working choice: component model baseline, record as source
claim: Contract records, not WIT, are the single source; the baseline is the component model with threads and GC out, until a feature survey says otherwise. Refuted if fewer than two independent engines ship it.

name: six contracts carry ten real shapes on paper
claim: Carry check on ten real harness shapes: 10 carried by the six contracts (6 clean, 4 after one field or operation each), 0 new contract. Weak: circular, surface unexercised, conformance still untested.

name: re-pointed handle replays as of a version
claim: A handle re-point is a new store version and a resolution records the version it read, so a past resolution replays; today points overwrite and the audit keeps only a hash in memory. Refuted if replay needs more than version and reader.

name: ids are platform-issued and recorded
claim: Opaque ids (handles, labels, run ids) come from identity.issue_id and are written to an event record, so replay reuses them instead of drawing new random ones. Refuted if a replay with recorded ids differs from the original.
